title: Steal This Computer Book: What They Won't Tell You About the Internet

description.main: Wallace Wang's 1998 handbook to hacker techniques and internet subculture, the first edition of a No Starch Press series. 340 pages.
description.extended:
Steal This Computer Book is Wallace Wang's 1998 handbook to hacker techniques and internet subculture, written for general readers.

The Library of Congress record lists 340 pages with an index and files the book under computer hackers and internet handbooks. A bookseller's description of this edition says it runs from eavesdropping and sabotage to protecting data and using the internet anonymously. It also points readers to where the actual programs can be found. It is the first of four editions from No Starch Press, which later issued Steal This Computer Book 2 (2000), 3 (2003) and 4.0 (2006).

Wang also wrote Steal This File Sharing Book for No Starch Press and works as a stand-up comic, according to the publisher. Its page for the fourth edition calls the book a national bestseller with more than 175,000 copies sold. It says that edition added coverage of spyware, rootkits and identity theft along with a companion CD of security and hacking programs.

notes: This is the 1998 first edition, the un-numbered title that came before the numbered editions. Later editions, all from No Starch Press: Steal This Computer Book 2 (2000, ISBN 9781886411425, 462 pages); Steal This Computer Book 3 (2003, ISBN 9781593270001, 359 pages); Steal This Computer Book 4.0 (May 2006, ISBN 9781593271053, 384 pages, with companion CD). The publisher link goes to the Library of Congress record for the 1998 edition, since No Starch Press's own page covers only the fourth edition. Identified from a spine photograph; edition not checked against the copy.
